newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell state shares in 130 firms soon.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell state shares in 130 firms soon.

text.p: Ukraine, trying to add life to a stalled privatisation programme, plans to sell shares in 130 state-owned enterprises in the near future, the deputy head of the State Property Fund said on Thursday.

Alexander Bondar told an international conference the state privatisation agency would sell shares in 11 companies on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange in early July, paving the way for their privatisation. He did not say which companies would be sold.

Ukrainian privatisation has been in the doldrums since the end of 1996, when parliament temporarily halted the process over quarrels about legislation. Bondar said privatisation had slowed for "objective and subjective reasons", but he did not explain.
He said the property fund was selling shares in mainly illiquid companies which had not found buyers at previous voucher-based auctions, in which citizens could trade certificates for company shares.
Ukraine plans to sell off 1,440 medium and large companies and about 3,400 small firms this year.
The struggling economy of the former Soviet republic has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence.
